newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt wins parliamentary confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt wins parliamentary confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday, clearing the way for the final segment of the 1997 budget to be converted into law.

Finanze Minister Vincenzo Visco called the do-or-die vote to sweep aside hundreds of opposition amendments to a package of measures which are designed to raise 4.3 trillion lire ($2.5 billion) in 1997.

The vote in the Chamber of Deputies, where Prodi depends on the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for support, was carried by 308 to 257, with one abstention, officials said. If a government loses a confidence motion it must resign.
Prodi's centre-left government called numerous confidence votes in both the upper and lower house of parliament last year to sidestep opposition filibustering.

Tuesday's vote covered a package of measures, introduced at the end of last year by cabinet decree, which included proposals to speed up payments of certain excise duties and incentives to boost the flagging car market.

The decree was tied to the 1997 budget bill, which aims to cut a total 62.5 trillion lire ($37.5 billion) off the deficit this year and was approved by parliament last December. ($ = 1666 Italian Lire)
